# fi-FI getuname

The Finnish Unicode character names of getuname.dll, which Character Map and
the other programs that name a character use: `dll/win32/getuname/lang/fi-FI.rc`
has all 37,966 names of en-US.rc, by the same ids, and `getuname.rc` includes it
under `LANGUAGE_FI_FI`. The names en-US.rc leaves empty stay empty.

The file is generated by [tools/getuname-fi](../../tools/getuname-fi/gen.py)
from en-US.rc. A Unicode name is a script, the kind of character, the letter's
own name and its modifiers, and Finnish puts an adjective before its noun as
English does, so the generator translates them in place with its glossary
(`gloss.py`) and a few rules where Finnish differs:

| English | Finnish |
|---------|---------|
| Latin Capital Letter A with Acute | Latinalainen iso kirjain A, jossa akuutti |
| Combining Dot Above | Yhdistävä piste yläpuolella |
| Devanagari Vowel Sign Aa | Devanagari-vokaalimerkki Aa |
| Hangul Syllable Ga | Hangul-tavu Ga |
| Rightwards Arrow from Bar | Oikealle osoittava nuoli palkista |
| Arabic Letter Beh Isolated Form | Arabialainen kirjain Beh, erillinen muoto |
| Kangxi Radical Water | Kangxi-radikaali vesi |

A letter's own name - a transliteration such as Beh, Ka or Kiyeok - is kept as
written; the diacritics use the terms of Finnish typography (akuutti, gravis,
treema, hattu, sedilji, makron). When upstream changes en-US.rc, run

    python3 -I tools/getuname-fi/gen.py <LiberNT>/dll/win32/getuname/lang/en-US.rc \
        <LiberNT>/dll/win32/getuname/lang/fi-FI.rc

and commit the result: `tests/real-upstream.sh` requires the file to be exactly
what the generator makes of the patched tree's en-US.rc, with the same ids.
